summary.text: Jonny Larsen, a Democratic Marine Corps combat veteran who grew up in Salt Lake City, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Utah's 4th Congressional District to Republican Rep. Mike Kennedy.
He later worked as a systems and network administrator.

paragraphs.text: Larsen grew up in a Salt Lake City trailer park; he says his mother placed him in a group home at age thirteen and that his grandmother then took him in.
He says he began working at twelve delivering newspapers for the Deseret News and was a night supervisor at Cinnabon by sixteen, and he graduated from West High School.
Larsen enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps at seventeen and served from 2000 to 2004.
He says he deployed to Iraq twice, with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines and then 3rd Battalion, 7th Marines, and fought in the Battle of Husaybah.
The Salt Lake Tribune describes him as a combat veteran who calls himself a "Blue Dog Democrat."
After leaving the Marines, Larsen built a career as a senior systems and network administrator in information technology.
He used the GI Bill to study applied math and physics at the University of Utah but, according to his candidate survey, ran out of funding before finishing.
He lives in Salt Lake City and says he is a VA patient and a cancer survivor treated by the VA.
During the campaign, he emphasized the cost of living, Medicare and Social Security, veterans' health care and banning stock trading by elected officials.
He received 38.9% of the vote to Mike Kennedy's 53.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
